title: mcp.json (MCP client server registry)

path.note: Two scopes, merged by WHOLE-SERVER REPLACEMENT: a workspace entry with the same server name replaces the global entry entirely (never a field-level merge).

notes: NO version field (same freeze rule as every other data file: contracts/data-files/index.json).

SECRETS: `env` / `headers` values are $VAR references resolved from the PROCESS environment at load time. A reference that cannot be resolved is a LOUD failure for that server (it is skipped and reported), never an empty string. The credential itself never lives in this file, so it is NOT marked `secret` and providers.json stays the only secret-bearing data file.
server names come from LOCAL configuration only — never from a remote serverInfo.name (untrusted, not unique across deployments, changes on upgrade).
DUPLICATE server name inside one file is a hard error, not 'last one wins'.
Crossed transport fields (command/args/env under `http`, url/headers under `stdio`) are a CONFIG ERROR, not something to ignore.
Defaults live HERE (the `default` keywords), not in prose; packages/mcp/src/types.ts re-asserts them against this file (schema-parity test).

servers.description: server name -> entry. The name is the tool-name prefix, so its character set is stricter than a tool name.

transport.description: P0: stdio (child process) or Streamable HTTP.

command.description: stdio only; the executable to spawn.

cwd.description: stdio only; working directory for the child process.

env.description: stdio only. Values are $VAR references resolved from the process environment. The child environment is the SCRUBBED parent environment (KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN shaped variables and CELESTEA_/DSH_ prefixed ones are dropped) merged with these explicit values.

url.description: http only; the endpoint. Operator configuration only — never derived from model output. The HTTP client does NOT follow redirects.

headers.description: http only. Values are $VAR references, same as `env`. Never echoed into any response or log line.

enabled.description: A disabled server is not connected and never appears on the model-facing tool surface.

approval.description: MCP tools need approval by DEFAULT; `never` is the explicit unattended opt-out. Per-tool overrides live in `tool_approval`.

tool_approval.description: per-tool override of `approval`, keyed by the server's own tool name.

timeout_ms.description: Budget for ONE tool call and for discovery, separately.

tool_allow.description: Optional narrowing. Matching is done against both the raw descriptor name and the model-visible name.

tool_deny.description: Applied AFTER tool_allow; deny wins. Same dual matching as tool_allow.

path_access.description: Declares the REAL path semantics of this server's tools. MCP tools land on the `write` floor otherwise (fail-closed), so a genuinely read-only tool must say so here.

reconnect.description: stdio only. HTTP never enters the reconnect supervisor: its transport recovers per request and there is no child process to relaunch.

max_attempts.description: Shared budget for one failure streak. It resets ONLY after a connection survives the stability window (= max_delay_ms), otherwise a server that crashes right after connecting would restart forever.

allOf.comment: http servers: url required, stdio fields forbidden.
Everything else (absent transport = stdio, the schema default): command required, http fields forbidden.

hardErrors.malformed: mcp.json '<path>' is malformed: {e} (startup fails; the unreadable file is never overwritten with an empty set)
hardErrors.duplicateServer: mcp.json '<path>' declares server '<name>' more than once (same-scope duplicates are a startup error, not 'last one wins')
hardErrors.unknownServerReference: mcp.json '<path>': server '<name>' references $VAR that is not set in the environment (the server is skipped and reported; it is never connected with an empty value)

durability: read-only for the engine (P0): the engine NEVER writes mcp.json; a missing/unparsable file is a hard error, never 'replaced with an empty set'.
roundTripRequirement: read -> write -> re-read: the package's serializer (packages/mcp/src/config.ts) round-trips this schema byte-for-byte (tests/mcp-config-roundtrip.test.ts).
